recent_posts.title: How to set up automated monitoring for breached data on the dark web
recent_posts.summary: A tutorial demonstrating how to set up automated monitoring systems to track breached and leaked personal data across the clear web, dark web, and Telegram, including usernames, passwords, and phone numbers.

recent_posts.title: Build a Dark Web Password Scanner
recent_posts.summary: A guide on building automated tools to monitor the clear web, dark web, and Telegram for leaked credentials and personal data from breaches. Covers both defensive use (protecting yourself) and offensive use in penetration testing engagements, enabling detection of compromised usernames, passwords, and phone numbers before malicious actors exploit them.

recent_posts.title: How to set up OpenClaw securely with Tailscale, HTTPS and firewall rules
recent_posts.summary: A guide to securing OpenClaw AI setups by avoiding root execution, hiding the service from the internet using Tailscale, enabling HTTPS, configuring strict firewall rules, switching to a privacy-focused model provider with uncensored models, replacing Telegram with an end-to-end encrypted messaging app, and mitigating prompt injection attacks through skill scanning.

recent_posts.title: How to set up OpenClaw AI agent for maximum security
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step guide to securing an OpenClaw AI agent deployment on a cloud server. Covers running as a non-root user, SSH key-based authentication with password login disabled, making the server invisible using Tailscale with strict firewall rules, enabling HTTPS via Tailscale Serve, switching to a privacy-focused AI model provider (Venice AI) to avoid data logging, replacing Telegram with Matrix for end-to-end encrypted messaging, setting up DM allowlists, scanning skills for malicious content, defending against prompt injection attacks, and running OpenClaw's built-in security audit tool.

recent_posts.title: AI agent automates penetration testing from a mobile phone
recent_posts.summary: A demonstration of an AI agent called OpenClaw that automates penetration testing tasks via mobile phone. The agent spawns sub-agents to gather OSINT on a target and run a full pentest on a website, returning detailed vulnerability reports including SQL injection findings and cracked passwords — all without manually executing commands or opening a laptop.

recent_posts.title: Set up an AI hacking assistant accessible via WhatsApp using Kali Linux
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough on setting up an AI-powered hacking assistant accessible via messaging apps like WhatsApp or Telegram. Using OpenClaw and Kali Linux, the setup allows users to send natural language commands and receive results such as discovering nearby CCTV cameras. The guide is presented as a step-by-step tutorial via a YouTube video.

recent_posts.title: How to set up an AI hacking agent with OpenClaw and Kali Linux
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step walkthrough for setting up OpenClaw, an agentic AI framework, on a cloud-hosted Kali Linux machine to create a personal AI hacking assistant. The guide covers provisioning a Kali VPS on Hostinger, securing SSH access with key-based authentication, installing and configuring OpenClaw, linking it to an LLM via OpenRouter (with Claude Opus recommended for agentic tasks), and connecting it to Telegram for mobile control. Practical demos show the agent autonomously finding nearby CCTV cameras, running OSINT investigations, and conducting web penetration tests using sub-agents and tools like Nmap, Metasploit, and the Strix framework—all controlled via phone without typing a single command.

recent_posts.title: Deploy uncensored AI models on cloud with Ollama
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to deploy uncensored AI models on cloud infrastructure using Ollama and Open WebUI. The tutorial covers finding uncensored models on Hugging Face, filtering by parameters and compatibility, and deploying them on Hostinger VPS. It demonstrates installing multiple models including Qwen 3 Coder (30B parameters) and a reasoning model, then using them to generate code without content restrictions. The setup allows access from any device via web browser, with all computation happening on the cloud server.

recent_posts.title: AI Prompt Injection
recent_posts.summary: Prompt injection is identified as the top security threat facing large language models (LLMs) according to OWASP. This attack technique allows hackers to manipulate AI systems to reveal sensitive information or bypass safety guardrails. The vulnerability is particularly concerning because AI models are non-deterministic, making prompt injection attacks difficult to prevent. As companies increasingly integrate AI into their operations, this creates new attack vectors for cybercriminals targeting organizational systems.
